stages.request: Heading ids clash with other ids on the pages we embed marklite output into: a heading called "Search" gets `id="search"`, the same id as our site's search box. Give heading ids a prefix, `section-` by default, so `# Search` becomes `id="section-search"`. Add an `id_prefix` option so users of the library can choose their own prefix, or pass an empty string to get the bare slugs they get today.

Rendered text is full of `"`: `She said "hi"` comes out as `She said "hi"`, which makes our HTML diffs noisy and is not needed in text. Leave double quotes as a plain `"` in text content (paragraphs, headings, list items, code). `&`, `<` and `>` must still be escaped, in text and in attribute values alike, and a `"` inside an attribute value must still come out as `"`.

The table of contents is too long on our bigger pages. By default it should list only level 1 and level 2 headings, so `toc_max_level` defaults to 2 instead of 3. Deeper levels must still be available to anyone who asks for them explicitly.

Rendering a file with very deeply nested block quotes crashes: one of our users pasted a line starting with a few thousand `>` characters and got a Python `RecursionError` traceback, both from `render()` and from the `marklite` command. Cap nesting with a `max_nesting` limit of 32 levels, counting block quotes and list items together. Anything deeper should raise `MarkliteError` with the message `nesting deeper than 32 levels` and its `line` set to the line where the too-deep block starts, and the command should report it like any other error.

Add strikethrough: `~~text~~` should render as `text`. It should combine with the other inline styles the way emphasis does (`~~**old**~~` gives `old`), and a single `~`, or three in a row, stays literal text.

`marklite.toc()` returns a flat list of entries, and everyone who builds a menu from it has to re-nest the entries by `level` themselves. Return a tree instead: the list of outermost entries, each entry with a `children` list holding the entries directly beneath it (an entry goes under the closest earlier entry with a lower level). Entries keep their `level`, `title` and `anchor`; an entry with nothing beneath it has an empty `children` list.
